title: Matthew 24 and "This Generation"
author: Thomas Ice
summary: Argues that 'all these things' in Matthew 24:34 are the events of the future Great Tribulation, so 'this generation' is the one that witnesses them.

title: The Key Fob to Olivet
author: Kenneth L. Gentry Jr.
summary: Reads Matthew 23:36 as the interpretive key to 24:34, placing the events of 24:4-34 within Jesus' own generation.

title: The First Resurrection (Westminster Theological Journal 37:3)
author: Meredith G. Kline
summary: Argues that 'first' (protos) in Revelation 20 marks a difference in kind, so the first resurrection is not bodily.

title: The First Resurrection: A Reaffirmation (Westminster Theological Journal 39:1)
author: Meredith G. Kline
summary: Kline's reply to J. Ramsey Michaels, defending the implied first death / second resurrection pairing.

title: The First Resurrection: A Response (Westminster Theological Journal 39:1)
author: J. Ramsey Michaels
summary: Grants a qualitative sense to 'first' but disputes Kline's conclusion that the first resurrection is non-bodily.

title: Regnum Caelorum: Patterns of Millennial Thought in Early Christianity (2nd ed.)
author: Charles E. Hill
summary: Argues that non-chiliastic eschatology was early and widespread, and links chiliasm to an underworld view of the intermediate state.

title: Were the Fathers Amillennial? An Evaluation of Charles Hill's Regnum Caelorum (Bibliotheca Sacra 177)
author: Brian C. Collins
summary: Critiques Hill's thesis, especially the claimed link between chiliasm and the intermediate state, citing Irenaeus.

title: Reexamining the Evidence for Recapitulation in Rev 20:1-10 (Westminster Theological Journal 51:2)
author: R. Fowler White
summary: Argues that Revelation 20:7-10 recapitulates 19:11-21, so 20:1-6 describes the interadvent age.

title: Making Sense of Rev 20:1-10? Harold Hoehner versus Recapitulation (JETS 37:4)
author: R. Fowler White
summary: White's response to Harold Hoehner's premillennial critique of recapitulation; summarizes Hoehner's arguments.

title: Premillennialism in Revelation 20:4-6 (Bibliotheca Sacra 135)
author: Jack S. Deere
summary: Defends a sequential, premillennial reading of Revelation 20:4-6 and the bodily sense of the first resurrection.

title: The Covenant of the Seventieth Week
author: Meredith G. Kline
summary: Essay in The Law and the Prophets (ed. J. H. Skilton) reading Daniel 9:24-27 covenantally and christologically against the dispensational futurist reading.

title: Structure and Chronology of Daniel's 70 Weeks
author: Kenneth L. Gentry Jr.
summary: Argues for a continuous seventy weeks culminating in Christ's work and the AD 70 judgment.

title: The Seventieth Week: Daniel 9:24-27 (An Exposition of the Book of Daniel, Part 18)
author: Kim Riddlebarger
summary: Amillennial sermon-exposition of Daniel 9:24-27 reading the seventieth week christologically.

title: Chronological Aspects of the Life of Christ (ch. 6: Daniel's Seventy Weeks and New Testament Chronology)
author: Harold W. Hoehner
summary: Calculates the sixty-nine weeks from 444 BC to AD 33 using 360-day years; originally a Bibliotheca Sacra series (1973-75).
note: Existence and contents confirmed through library catalogues and journal indexes; no free online text located.

title: The Erosion of Postmillennialism in American Religious Thought, 1865-1925 (Church History 53)
author: James H. Moorhead
summary: Historian's account of how mainline postmillennialism faded into a general faith in progress.

title: Living in the Shadow of the Second Coming: American Premillennialism, 1875-1982 (enlarged ed.)
author: Timothy P. Weber
summary: Historical study of the rise and influence of dispensational premillennialism in America.
note: Existence confirmed through library catalogues and reviews (original edition 1979, covering 1875-1925).

title: Antichrist Before the Day of the Lord
author: Alan E. Kurschner
summary: Full-length defense of the prewrath rapture position: the church faces the Antichrist's persecution before the day of the Lord's wrath.
note: Existence confirmed through booksellers' listings (Eschatos Publishing).

title: The Church and the Tribulation
author: Robert H. Gundry
summary: Major scholarly defense of posttribulationism.

title: "The Church and the Tribulation": A Review (Bibliotheca Sacra 131)
author: Charles C. Ryrie
summary: Pretribulational review and critique of Gundry's posttribulationism.

title: Has the Church Replaced Israel? A Theological Evaluation
author: Michael J. Vlach
summary: Surveys supersessionism historically and argues for a future salvation and restoration of national Israel.

title: The Riddleblog: posts on the binding of Satan
author: Kim Riddlebarger
summary: Amillennial expositions arguing that the binding of Satan in Revelation 20 is a present reality since Christ's first coming.

title: The Binding of Satan in Revelation 20 (The Master's Seminary Journal 26:1)
author: Matt Waymeyer
summary: Argues the binding of Satan in Revelation 20:1-3 does not support amillennialism but a future millennium.

title: James White and 2 Timothy 3 (series)
author: Kenneth L. Gentry Jr.
summary: Gentry's multi-part reply to James White's use of 2 Timothy 3 against postmillennialism.

title: The Resurrection of Daniel 12: Future or Fulfilled?
author: Don K. Preston
summary: Argues that the resurrection of Daniel 12 (and so of 1 Corinthians 15) was fulfilled in connection with AD 70.
note: Existence confirmed through booksellers' listings; publication year approximate.

title: Understanding Dispensationalists (2nd ed.)
author: Vern S. Poythress
summary: Irenic covenant-theology critique of the dispensational 'literal' hermeneutic, written for dialogue.
